scenarios.name: single, pension below the $6,000 per-taxpayer cap -- Arkansas's employer-pension exclusion carries no age requirement, so this and the next case vary income rather than age
scenarios.source: 2025 Arkansas AR1000F/AR1000NR Instructions, 'PRIMARY EMPLOYER PENSION PLAN(S)/QUALIFIED IRA(s)' section, printed page 13, LINE 18A: 'If you had income from an employment-related pension plan or a qualified traditional IRA distribution, enter the gross amount(s) from box 1 of your 1099-R(s) in the space provided... You are entitled to a $6,000 exemption from the taxable amount; the balance is taxable to Arkansas.' The same page separately notes the $6,000 IRA-distribution exclusion applies only after age 59 1/2 ('the first $6,000 is exempt from tax' once the participant reaches that age) -- but that age condition is specific to the IRA-distribution half of line 18A, not the pension half ('You might be eligible for the $6,000 exemption for retirement or disability benefits provided the distribution was from public or private employment-related retirement systems... The recipient does not have to be retired.'). This fixture uses PENSION income only (no iraWithdrawals) to keep the case clean of that age-gated IRA sub-rule, matching how Arkansas's own form treats the two income types as one combined $6,000 cap on line 18A/18B rather than two independent caps -- the app's config models pensionExemption and iraWithdrawalExemption as SEPARATE $6,000 caps (pensionAndIRAShareSingleCap: false), which is a different, out-of-scope discrepancy from the per-taxpayer attribution this batch targets, so no case in this fixture mixes both income types. OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDING, not pinned as a knownDefect: the same instructions, 'Individual Income Tax Rate Reduction' note, printed page 6 (PDF page 6; corrected 2026-08-04 after a reviewer's page-footer check -- the printed-page label was miscopied as 5, the PDF page was already correct): 'Marginal Income Tax rates for 2025 are 3.9%, as amended in 2024' -- the top rate in TaxCalculationEngine's AR config is 3.7%, not 3.9%; this fixture computes against the CONFIGURED bracket table on both sides of the comparison so the only variable exercised is the per-taxpayer attribution this batch targets. Standard deduction $2,470 single (configured, and independently confirmed correct against the same instructions, printed page 14 (PDF page 14) table; corrected 2026-08-04 after a reviewer's page-footer check -- page 13 carries the LINE 18A pension-exclusion text quoted above, not the standard-deduction table, confirmed by direct pdftotext extraction). Arkansas taxable income = 4,000 - 2,470 = 1,530, already less than the $4,000 pension (which is itself under the $6,000 cap so fully excluded regardless), so taxable income after the exclusion floors at $0 and tax is $0.00.

scenarios.name: single, pension above the $6,000 per-taxpayer cap -- no age gate applies to the pension half of line 18A so a single filer's exclusion is unaffected by attribution
scenarios.source: Same AR1000F Instructions, LINE 18A, printed page 13 (see prior case for the full quote). Pension $20,000 exceeds the $6,000 cap, so $6,000 is excluded regardless of attribution. Standard deduction $2,470 single (configured) and the single bracket table (0%/$0, 2%/$5,600, 3%/$11,200, 3.4%/$16,000, 3.7%/$26,400) are the CONFIGURED StateTaxData.swift values; see the prior case's out-of-scope finding on the real 3.9% top rate this fixture deliberately does not substitute. Arkansas taxable income = 20,000 - 2,470 - 6,000 = 11,530. tax = 0*5,600 + 0.02*(11,200-5,600) + 0.03*(11,530-11,200) = 112.00 + 9.90 = 121.90.

scenarios.name: MFJ, BOTH spouses individually have qualifying pension income above Arkansas's own $6,000-per-taxpayer cap -- the load-bearing case for this batch, isolating the missing exemptionAppliesPerIndividual flag
scenarios.source: Same instructions, LINE 18A/18B, printed page 13: LINE 18A covers the PRIMARY's own pension/IRA income and its own $6,000 exemption; 'LINE 18B... If filing status 2, Married Filing Joint, spouse must enter the taxable amount on line 18B, column A' -- a separate line for the spouse's OWN income, gated by the SAME $6,000 exemption applied to the primary's line 18A, i.e. two independent $6,000 exemptions on a joint return, not one household-wide $6,000. Scenario: primary receives $15,000 from a private employer pension, spouse separately receives $15,000 from her own former employer's pension, pooled pensionIncome = $30,000. Correct exclusion = $6,000 (primary, capped) + $6,000 (spouse, capped) = $12,000. Standard deduction $4,940 married and the married bracket table are the CONFIGURED values (see case 1's out-of-scope finding). Arkansas taxable income = 30,000 - 4,940 - 12,000 = 13,060. tax = 0.02*5,600 + 0.03*(11,200-5,600) + 0.034*(13,060-11,200) = 112.00 + 55.80 = 167.80.

knownDefect.summary: exemptionAppliesPerIndividual is false, so StateTaxData.swift's AR config applies the $6,000 cap once household-wide instead of once per taxpayer, halving the correct $12,000 MFJ exclusion when both spouses independently qualify. PHASE 5 WARNING: expectedStateTax in every case of this fixture is computed against the CONFIGURED bracket table (top rate 3.7%), not Arkansas's real published top rate of 3.9% (see the out-of-scope finding in case 1's source string). Fixing exemptionAppliesPerIndividual alone will turn this case green, but Arkansas will still be wrong for every filer whose income reaches the top bracket. Green here does NOT mean Arkansas is correct.

scenarios.name: MFJ, only ONE spouse has pension income -- the case that stops a naive doubling fix, because today's single-cap engine happens to land on the correct total here even though its reasoning is wrong
scenarios.source: Same instructions, LINE 18A/18B, printed page 13. Scenario: primary receives $25,000 from a single employer pension; spouse has no pension or IRA income of her own this year, so her own line 18B is $0 regardless of any cap. Correct law: only the primary's own income is eligible, capped at her individual $6,000; the household total is $6,000 whether or not a doubled cap exists, because there is no second income to which it could apply. This matches today's flag-off engine (min(25,000, $6,000 single household cap) = $6,000) exactly, and that coincidence is why this case matters: a Phase 5 fix that sets exemptionAppliesPerIndividual = true without also checking which spouse actually earned the pooled pension dollars would double the cap to $12,000 for a couple in this exact shape (both spouses independently clear the age-59 fallback in TaxCalculationEngine.swift's ageQualifiesForExemption) and erroneously shelter income the non-earning spouse never had. Standard deduction $4,940 married (CONFIGURED; see case 1's out-of-scope finding). Arkansas taxable income = 25,000 - 4,940 - 6,000 = 14,060. tax = 112.00 + 0.03*(14,060-11,200) = 112.00 + 85.80 = 197.80.
